subject.title: Containerized/self-hosted deploys can't use externalized channel plugins: openKeyedStore is gated to trusted plugins, with no supported way to trust a self-hosted channel

question: What provenance and storage contract should official external plugins use in immutable/container deployments where the active OpenClaw home is mounted over image-baked state?
rationale: The source confirms the runtime can only safely grant keyed-store access from trusted install provenance, but current Docker/state layout gives no supported way to preserve that provenance for image-baked official plugins.

options.title: Add immutable official plugin provenance
options.body: Support a build-time official install root or importable signed install record that runtime verifies against the official catalog while keeping raw load paths untrusted.

options.title: Document mounted-state installs only
options.body: Keep the current security boundary unchanged and document that self-hosted operators must install official plugins into the mounted OpenClaw state before runtime starts.

options.title: Accept explicit operator trust
options.body: Add an operator allowlist or trusted flag that bypasses provenance for configured plugin paths, accepting a broader security tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Add immutable official plugin provenance
recommendation.body: Support a build-time official install root or importable signed install record that runtime verifies against the official catalog while keeping raw load paths untrusted.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned on the issue and have recent merged history around adjacent plugin trust-boundary enforcement.
